results.title: AMC rising in a process bay
results.text: Compare AMC at the make-up air inlet with AMC in the bay. If the inlet is steady while the bay rises, the chemical filtration stage is the likely source.

results.title: Chemical filter breakthrough
results.text: Chemical filter media loads up over time. Near the end of rated life, contaminants break through into the supply air. Check filter runtime against its rated life and the differential pressure history. Corrective action: replace the filter media and verify AMC in the bay afterwards.

report.narrative: An investigation was conducted for AMC in litho bay exceeding the upper limit of 1.0 ppbv, with a measured reading of 1.7851 ppbv. The rate of change analysis from E2 showed a slope of 0.4943 ppbv per hour over 120 minutes. Upstream tracing via E8 identified CHEM_FILTER_01 and MAU_01. Sensor data from E9 for AMC_MAU_IN showed a stable mean of 0.5014 ppbv, while E3 showed bay levels rising up to 1.7851 ppbv. According to E7, CHEM_FILTER_01 has reached 6930 hours out of a rated 7000 hours, representing 99.0 percent of its rated life. Knowledge base citations AMC-01 and AMC-02 indicate that when the inlet is steady while the bay rises, chemical filtration is the likely source, and near the end of rated life, contaminants break through into the supply air.
recommended_actions: Recommend that a qualified engineer review the chemical filter runtime on CHEM_FILTER_01 currently at 6930 hours against its 7000 rated hours.
Recommend that a qualified engineer replace the chemical filter media and verify AMC in the bay afterwards.
